name: Devi
realName: Tara Mehta (modern host of the Devi entity)
summary: A warrior-goddess force reborn in a young woman named Tara Mehta, in a gangster-ruled Indian city. Shekhar Kapur's Devi was a flagship of Virgin Comics' Shakti line and loosely echoes Durga.
origin: Devi is a celestial warrior created by the gods to fight the renegade god Bala. She beat him in hand-to-hand combat, and the supreme lord Bodha then blinded, captured and imprisoned him in the hidden fortress Jwala. The entity first appeared inside a warrior-woman of the Durapasya, a clan of human warriors of light. When Bala threatens the universe again, Devi is reborn in Tara Mehta, a wealthy and unaware young woman living in Sitapur, a city ruled by gangsters.
powers: Superhuman strength and fighting skill as an incarnate warrior goddess
Channelling of the energy of human prayer
Reincarnation: the Devi entity is reborn into new human hosts
Leads armies of gods and humans in battle

storyline.title: A goddess for a new line
storyline.beat: Issue 1 appears in July 2006 as one of Virgin Comics' first books, opening with the original Devi's war against the renegade god Bala.

storyline.title: Tara Mehta
storyline.beat: The series follows Tara Mehta, an unawakened host, as the assassin Kratha, her gangster boyfriend Iyam and a police inspector with a hidden sixth sense circle her before the Devi entity wakes.

storyline.title: Three scripters
storyline.beat: Siddharth Kotian opens the series, Samit Basu writes issues 3 to 10, and Saurav Mohapatra takes over from issue 11 through to the 2008 finish.

storyline.title: Witchblade/Devi
storyline.beat: Top Cow and Virgin pair Devi with Witchblade in a two-part crossover, published April and May 2008.

storyline.title: Devi: Rebirth
storyline.beat: Graphic India brings the character back as Devi: Rebirth in 2016, following another crossover with Witchblade.

gossip.text: Tara's wealthy boyfriend Iyam is secretly one of Bala's old generals and now the top ganglord of Sitapur.
Ron Marz, then the writer of Witchblade, wrote the Top Cow half of the Witchblade/Devi crossover.
Virgin Comics grew out of an Indian-set Spider-Man comic from 2004, and it was backed by Richard Branson and Deepak Chopra.
Many of Virgin's artists were former street artists and temple painters from a Bangalore studio.
Devi is just a comic retelling of the Durga story.
gossip.truth: It is only loosely based on Durga. The comic invents its own gods, clans and a gangster-ruled city.

gossip.text: Early reviewers found Devi's first two issues thin on world-building, but felt issue 3 fixed the problems.

quiz.q: Which filmmaker is credited as the creator of Devi?
quiz.why: Shekhar Kapur created Devi for Virgin Comics' Shakti line.

quiz.q: Which mythological goddess is Devi loosely based on?
quiz.why: The character is loosely modelled on the warrior goddess Durga.

quiz.q: Which Top Cow heroine crossed over with Devi in 2008?
quiz.why: Top Cow and Virgin published the Witchblade/Devi crossover in April and May 2008.

quiz.q: What is the name of the fire-and-stone fortress where Bala is imprisoned?
quiz.why: Bodha locked Bala away in Jwala, a fortress hidden deep underground.

theme.tagline: A warrior goddess wakes in a city of neon and gangsters.

timeline.title: Devi #1
timeline.note: Devi debuts in July 2006 as a Shakti-line launch title from Virgin Comics, created by Shekhar Kapur.

timeline.title: First paperback
timeline.note: The first collected volume, issues 1 to 5, comes out in June 2007.

timeline.title: Witchblade crossover
timeline.note: Top Cow and Virgin publish Witchblade/Devi and Devi/Witchblade in April and May.

timeline.title: Liquid Comics
timeline.note: On 24 September 2008 Virgin Comics is renamed Liquid Comics after a management buyout.

timeline.title: Graphic India focus
timeline.note: In February Liquid Comics refocuses on Graphic India, the digital comics start-up that later relaunches Devi.

timeline.title: Devi: Rebirth
timeline.note: Graphic India relaunches the character in August 2016 after a January crossover with Witchblade.

facts.text: Virgin Comics traces its roots to an Indian-set Spider-Man comic launched in 2004, which the founders then built into a whole line of Indian-flavoured comics.
Much of the line's artwork came from a Bangalore studio, and several of its artists had earlier worked as street artists and temple painters.
Tara's boyfriend Iyam hides a huge secret: he was once Bala's favourite general and now runs Sitapur's gangs, including a nightclub called the Abyss.
Kratha is an apsara, a heavenly being, who works as an assassin; Lord Bala hires her through a woman named Amara to kill Tara before she awakens, but the Durapasya kidnap and drug Kratha first.
Agantuk is a priest of the Durapasya who pushes the radical idea of keeping the human host alive for the Devi entity, and he is largely the reason Tara survives when Devi stirs inside her.
The key to Bala's sarcophagus prison was entrusted to the Gatekeeper, a creature made of fire and stone.
In the comic, Inspector Rahul Singh's supernatural sense is so overactive that he dulls it with drink, which makes him a burnt-out cop until he ends up as Tara's sidekick.

The Witchblade/Devi crossover, announced on 27 February 2008, was billed as the first between the two publishers and paired Sara Pezzini, a New York detective who carries the Witchblade, with Devi, reborn in Tara Mehta.
Wikipedia says that in sales terms Devi was the most popular comic of Virgin's Shakti line, even though its early issues drew some criticism for thin world-building.
Ron Marz was the editor of three Shakti books, Devi, Ramayan 3392 A.D. and The Sadhu, and joined Virgin about a year before the crossover to mentor its young India-based creators.

The Witchblade crossover came in two parts: Witchblade/Devi #1 from Top Cow in April 2008, then Devi/Witchblade #1 from Virgin in May, written by Samit Basu and drawn by Mukesh Singh, with Greg Land variant covers on both.
Shakti, a word for 'power', was Virgin's imprint for Indian content; its Director's Cut line let filmmakers incubate new properties, such as John Woo's.
Virgin's Shakti launch lineup was four books: Devi, The Sadhu (a raj-era tale written by Gotham Chopra), Snake Woman and Ramayan Reborn.
Publishers Weekly described Devi at launch as the story of a young woman with mystical powers who tries to clean up a corrupt city.
Shekhar Kapur, who created Devi, was also one of the founders of Virgin Comics, alongside Richard Branson, Deepak Chopra, Sharad Devarajan, Suresh Seetharaman and Gotham Chopra.
Virgin's founders hoped to blend classic Indian mythology and spiritual themes with modern comic imagery; Gotham Chopra said they wanted to deal in universal themes.
A review of Devi: Rebirth #1 says the story has roots in the Mahabharata and Ramayana, with a cataclysmic war that recalls Kurukshetra, and that Devi is apparently based on the goddess Durga.
In Devi: Rebirth #1 the gods seal Bala in a stone tomb after the ancient war, and in the present day he sits in an office, looking human behind sunglasses.
Devi beat Bala hand-to-hand and blinded him; Bodha, the supreme lord of creation, then imprisoned him in Jwala, a fortress of fire and stone hidden deep within the earth.
In August 2008 Virgin Comics restructured and moved from New York to Los Angeles, and the company was renamed Liquid Comics.
Gotham Chopra said India had no real tradition of comics publishing, but a growing web of small neighbourhood shops serving young readers could be an outlet for Virgin's books.

kidSummary: Devi is a warrior goddess force who is reborn in a young woman named Tara. When an old rebel god named Bala threatens the world again, Devi wakes up to protect people with fire and courage.

story.title: A rebel god
story.text: Long ago a god named Bala turned against the others. The gods made a warrior called Devi to stop him.

story.title: Bala is locked away
story.text: Devi beat Bala in a fight, and the supreme lord Bodha locked him inside a hidden fortress named Jwala.

story.title: Meet Tara
story.text: In the gangster-ruled city of Sitapur, a young woman named Tara Mehta has no idea that Devi's power is sleeping inside her.

story.title: Devi wakes
story.text: When Bala's plans return, helpers and enemies gather around Tara, and Devi awakens to fight for human prayers and hope.

story.title: A new start
story.text: Years later the character returned in Devi: Rebirth, and once teamed up with Witchblade, a hero from another comic company.
